pages.title: Frontispiece
pages.text: The Ember of Duat is not a spark to be spent casually. It only answers those who have truly read the inscriptions. $(br2)Study the pages, then right-click the ember to open its dedicated comparison panel. Only the right name will make the fire lean toward you.

The trial comes in three waves. The hostile ranks are highlighted, and a boss bar records how many remain. $(br2)Finish all three and the first reversal of the Regent's Crown finally loosens. If the trial breaks midway, the ember falls silent and a whole new cycle of inscriptions must be solved.

pages.title: How to Read
pages.text: These lines are not meant to be translated stroke by stroke. They are a veil, hiding the true name behind title and image. $(br2)Look at names such as the sun-wheel, the great river, the twin crown, or the white feather, then think of the ancient thing that rises first to mind.

The ember does not ask for perfect scholarship or literal decoding. It listens only for the true name hidden inside the shadow. $(br2)Once you have a guess, open the ember's input panel and enter it there. A wrong answer earns no explanation. A right one bends the fire to your side.

pages.title: Example
pages.text: Take the inscription of the sun-wheel. $(br2)Ignore the cipher-shapes at first and focus on the title. Then follow the Egyptian image that fits most directly: the thing crossing the sky by day and lending its rhythm to every clock of the world.

So the reasoning is simple: $(br)sun-wheel -> the sun in the sky -> enter "sun" in the ember panel. $(br2)The rest follow the same method: grasp the title first, trace the image second, and finally enter the single nearest accepted English answer.

Once the undead host falls silent, the fragment will no longer be printed inside the manual. The fuller ash-fragment now surfaces in the Ember of Duat interface itself, where the sentence is meant to be pieced back together.
